name: Well-differentiated liposarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and molecular diagnostic criteria for well-differentiated liposarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of mature adipocytes with atypical stromal cells and fibrous septa
MDM2 gene amplification detected by FISH or PCR
Imaging showing well-circumscribed fatty mass with thick septa and nodular non-adipose areas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of atypical adipocytes with MDM2 amplification
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MDM2 amplification is critical to distinguish from benign lipomas

laboratory: Possible mild anemia if large tumor causes chronic blood loss
imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed fatty mass with thickened septa
CT scan demonstrating low-density lipomatous tumor with nodular non-adipose components
other: Histopathology revealing mature adipocytes with atypical stromal cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for MDM2 and CDK4 proteins

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of atypical stromal cells on histology
Typically smaller, softer, and more superficial
Presence of high-grade non-lipogenic sarcomatous areas
Rapid tumor growth and metastasis potential

redFlags: New onset of pain or neurological symptoms
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition, 2020
Fletcher CDM, et al. Diagnostic Histopathology of Tumors, 4th Edition, 2013
